text: When Claude heads the wrong way, press Esc to stop it right away, then say what to do instead
In the terminal, press Esc twice on an empty prompt to undo Claude's last steps: code, chat, or both
In the terminal, press Shift+Tab to switch to accept-edits mode instead of approving each edit
Type @ and start a file path to attach the real file instead of describing what's in it
Start a message with ! to run a shell command yourself, handy for logins and quick checks
When you start an unrelated task, run /clear so the old task's context doesn't skew answers
/context shows what is filling the context window when answers start getting sloppy
/btw <question> answers a side question without adding it to the conversation history
/add-dir <path> lets Claude read and edit a second folder or repo in the same session
Old sessions aren't lost after /clear: /resume reopens any of them, so start fresh freely
To keep a long task going when context fills up, run /compact to summarize history and carry on
When you correct Claude on the same thing twice, add the rule as one line in your CLAUDE.md
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md applies to every project, so put your OS and style preferences there once
/init drafts a CLAUDE.md from your codebase, so a new project starts with notes to edit
.claude/settings.local.json holds settings just for you in this repo and stays out of git
Type / to list every skill and command you already have before you build something new
Before you build a skill or hook from scratch, check /plugin; a ready-made one may exist
To make a skill run only when you call it, add disable-model-invocation: true to its frontmatter
To stop retyping a prompt, save it as .claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md and run it as /<name>
Before a big search across many files, add "use subagents" so the noise stays out of your context
Two unrelated tasks run better in two separate sessions than sharing one context window
A rule you repeat in chat can be forgotten; /hooks lets the harness enforce it every time
/schedule sets up a routine that runs a recurring check for you, like a morning summary
/loop 5m <prompt> re-runs a check every 5 minutes, useful while waiting on CI or a deploy
/model switches models mid-session, so simple tasks don't have to run on your biggest model
When the same fix fails twice, switch to a stronger model with /model instead of re-prompting
/effort high makes Claude think longer before replying when a hard problem gets a shallow answer
/fast turns on faster output while keeping the same model, for when you want Opus sooner
When Claude names an exact API, flag, or version, ask it to quote the doc lines it's based on
To check a doubtful answer, ask the same question in a fresh session and compare the two
For fewer confident guesses, add "If you're unsure, say so" as a line in your CLAUDE.md
Before you accept new code, ask Claude to run the tests or the build, not just read it
/diff shows exactly what changed in your working tree, so you can check before trusting "done"
Before a big change, commit first so undoing it is a single git command
claude --worktree <name> starts a risky experiment in its own checkout, leaving main untouched
When two corrections haven't fixed it, run /clear and start over with a more specific prompt
/usage shows how much of your usage a session consumed, worth a look after heavy work
To fix a result that missed, say exactly what was wrong instead of resending the same request
One pasted example of the output you want beats a whole paragraph describing the format
A reason like "keep it fast, it runs on every keystroke" lets Claude make the right calls
To phrase a request better, ask Claude to rewrite your prompt and explain what it changed
Paste a screenshot with Ctrl+V (Alt+V on Windows) instead of describing a visual bug in words
MCP server not working? /mcp shows which servers are connected and which need sign-in
claude -p "<prompt>" runs Claude once and prints the result, ready for scripts and CI
A subagent can't see this chat, so give it file paths and say what a good answer looks like
Before Claude plans changes in unfamiliar code, ask it to read and summarize the code first
Closed the terminal by accident? claude --continue reopens the last session in this folder
In the terminal, press Ctrl+R to search your prompt history and reuse an earlier prompt
In the terminal, press Ctrl+G to write a long prompt in your own text editor instead
In the terminal, Ctrl+S stashes your draft so you can ask something else; press it again to restore
In the terminal, press Ctrl+B to send a long-running command to the background and keep working
In the terminal, press Ctrl+T to show or hide Claude's task checklist during a big task
In the terminal, press Ctrl+O to open the full transcript and see exactly what Claude ran and read
You can type while Claude works: press Enter and your message is queued for the next turn
/branch copies the conversation so you can try another direction without losing this one
/subtask <task> hands a side job to a subagent and brings only the result back here
/background detaches this session to keep running; check on it later with claude agents
/rename <name> labels this session so you can find it quickly later in /resume
/recap gives a one-line summary of where this session stands, handy after a break
/copy puts Claude's last answer on your clipboard; /copy 2 grabs the one before it
/cd <path> moves this whole session to another folder without losing the conversation
/export <file> saves the whole conversation as plain text, ready to share or archive
Before you open a PR, run /code-review to check the changes for bugs; add --fix to apply fixes
/simplify reviews your changes for cleanup and applies it; it doesn't hunt for bugs
When a change touches auth, user input, or secrets, run /security-review on the branch
/batch <instruction> splits a change across many files into parallel agents in worktrees
New worktree missing your .env? List it in .worktreeinclude to copy it into each one
To slim down a long CLAUDE.md, move sections into files and pull them in with @path/to/file
Rules in .claude/rules/ with a paths: field load only when Claude works on matching files
Rewind can't undo rm, mv, or cp run in Bash, so commit before Claude deletes files
Terminal flickering on long output? /tui fullscreen switches to the flicker-free renderer
In the terminal, /statusline adds a status bar below the prompt, for example showing model and context
Shift+Enter won't add a new line in VS Code or Cursor? /terminal-setup installs the keybinding
Coming from Codex, Gemini CLI, or Cursor? /import brings your existing configuration over
/remote-control lets you continue this session from claude.ai when you step away from your desk
/config <key>=<value> changes a setting in one line without opening the settings menu
claude -p --bare skips your hooks, skills, and CLAUDE.md so CI runs stay repeatable
In the desktop app, press Ctrl+Shift+M (Cmd+Shift+M on Mac) to switch permission mode mid-session
In the desktop app, press Ctrl+/ (Cmd+/ on Mac) to see every keyboard shortcut the Code tab supports
In the desktop app, press Ctrl+; (Cmd+; on Mac) to open a side chat that can read the main thread
